stories.title: The Plan: With a Big Vacancy Looming, Durst Goes Big on Renovating 114 West 47th
stories.excerpt: Situated just off Sixth Avenue is 114 West 47th Street, a 26-story office building owned by the Durst Organization that is undergoing a major renovation. By 2029, this 600,000-square-foot Midtown Manhattan office asset will be equipped with a shining new lobby, high-quality tenant amenities, private terraces on seven floors, elevators, new chillers and other building system upgrades. The building also will feature office environments with ceiling heights between 12 and 14 feet, floor plates running between 18,000 and 32,000 square feet, and an abundance of natural light. “Durst built the building in 1989, and since then U.S. Trust — which was then bought by Charles Schwab, which was then bought by Merrill Lynch, which was then bought by Bank of America — has always occupied the lion’s share of the base of the building,” said Eric Engelhardt, senior vice president of commercial leasing at Durst. “Their lease will expire in the early part of 2028, and that has prompted us to bring nearly the entire building to market.” The four office tenants and one retail tenant currently in the building will remain during the renovations. “114 West 47th Street presents a rare moment for visionary companies to position themselves in prime Midtown with a renovated, world-class work environment,” Jody Durst, president of the Durst Organization, said in a statement announcing the renovation. In the lobby, Durst and architect HOK plan to add gray granite floors and concave paneled white oak walls, as well as soft seating to provide some tranquility and calmness for those arriving from the chaos of Sixth Avenue. “The original lobby was designed in the `80s, and it was really at the pinnacle of Postmodernism, and there was a lot of multi-use of stone,” said Kenneth Drucker, design principal at HOK. “There were three formal rooms, basically an entry vestibule, and then three spaces before you got to the elevator lobby. bullets: Durst Organization renovating 600K SF Midtown Manhattan office by 2029

stories.summary: Durst Organization is investing heavily to renovate 114 West 47th, a 600,000-square-foot Midtown Manhattan office tower, adding a new lobby, 2,500-SF tenant lounge, private terraces on seven floors, upgraded HVAC, and improved ceiling heights (12–14 feet) and floor plates (18K–32K SF). Work concludes by 2029. The developer is retaining all current tenants during construction, signaling confidence in the asset's marketability post-upgrade.
stories.impact: This is a defensive value-play in Midtown office, not a demand signal. Durst's investment reflects the need to compete for tenants in a soft market; large-scale renovations to secure occupancy indicate ongoing Manhattan office softness and the cost burden on developers to differentiate supply. Multifamily developers should note Midtown's oversupply and tenant competition, which may suppress office worker in-migration and nearby residential demand.

stories.title: Sky Equity Goes Vertical on Tribeca Condos
stories.excerpt: Sky Equity Group, the New York City-based real estate development firm founded by Simon Dushinsky, has launched vertical construction at 65 Franklin St., an upcoming luxury condominium in Manhattan’s Tribeca neighborhood. With foundation work complete, the 24-story tower is rising above the corner of Franklin Street and Broadway. The building broke ground in April and sales are slated to launch next year. “We’re pleased to reach this important construction milestone at 65 Franklin Street as we continue expanding our condominium portfolio in Manhattan,” said Dushinsky. “Thoughtfully designed to complement Tribeca’s distinctive architecture and historic streetscape, 65 Franklin will be a meaningful addition to the neighborhood while delivering an exceptional residential offering for future homeowners.” In 2025, Sky Equity secured a $320-million construction loan with G4 Capital Partners for the ground-up condominium. Sky Equity Group also acquired 65 Franklin’s neighboring site, 59 Franklin St., from Bonjour Capital and air rights from 361 Broadway, a landmarked building across the street, for the development. Following a restructuring and recapitalization with HAP Investments in 2025, Sky Equity became the project’s sole developer. Where the apartment industry connects. stories.summary: Sky Equity Group has begun vertical construction on 65 Franklin Street, a 24-story luxury condominium in Tribeca with foundation complete and sales launching in 2026. The developer secured a $320 million construction loan from G4 Capital Partners in 2025 and acquired adjacent land and air rights to maximize the site. The project reflects continued condo confidence in core Manhattan despite broader affordability concerns.
stories.impact: Construction capital remains available for trophy Manhattan residential in high-demand submarkets; G4 Capital's $320M loan signals lender comfort with luxury Manhattan condo risk despite recent market volatility. Tribeca supply pipeline remains elevated; multifamily developers competing in Manhattan should monitor luxury condo starts, as condo absorption may cannibalize rental demand in nearby buildings, particularly for younger affluent cohorts.

stories.title: Paragon Acquires Grocery-Anchored Shopping Center from Long-Term Owners
stories.excerpt: Paragon Commercial Group has completed the off-market acquisition of a grocery-anchored shopping center in the Tujunga neighborhood of Los Angeles. Located on Foothill Boulevard in northeastern Los Angeles along the foothills of the San Gabriel mountains, the 46,055 square-foot property was acquired from the family of the original developer that had owned and operated the property for more than six decades. Greg Offsay and Caleb Morrison of illi Commercial Real Estate brokered the transaction, marking the second off-market deal Paragon has made in as many months. The nearly 2.7-acre center is anchored by Smart & Final, a tenant of more than 30 years, and Goodwill, which has occupied the property for 25 years. “This acquisition is right in the strike zone for Paragon because it is an irreplaceable, grocery-anchored center with decades of tenant loyalty that will benefit from Paragon’s unique hands-on management and leasing structure,” said Mark Harrigian, co-founder and principal of Los Angeles-based Paragon. “Purchasing from long-term owners gives our team the ability to bring a fresh perspective and fresh capital to the property, while preserving the anchor tenancy that has been a foundation of this community for a generation.” Paragon plans to upgrade physical attributes of the center to better reflect the surrounding community, including the common area, building facades, lighting and signage. bullets: Paragon Commercial acquired 46K SF grocery-anchored center, Tujunga/Foothill Boulevard, Los Angeles

stories.summary: Paragon Commercial Group completed an off-market acquisition of a 46,055-square-foot grocery-anchored shopping center in Tujunga, northeastern Los Angeles, anchored by Smart & Final (30+ years) and Goodwill (25 years). The nearly 2.7-acre property was purchased from the original developer's family, who had owned it for over six decades. Paragon plans to apply hands-on management and leasing expertise to unlock value while preserving anchor stability.
stories.impact: Limited direct relevance to multifamily development. However, grocery-anchored retail resilience in secondary Los Angeles neighborhoods (Tujunga) indicates stable foot traffic and community demand; multifamily developers underwriting nearby infill or mixed-use projects should view grocery anchor strength as a positive demand co-signal for residential absorption in submarkets with entrenched retail anchors.

stories.title: Sterling Organization Nears Delivery of High-Bay Bronx Warehouse
stories.excerpt: JLL has begun marketing 307 Bruckner, a newly developed 100,000-square-foot industrial property in the Bronx. Developed by the Sterling Organization and scheduled for delivery in the third quarter of 2026, 307 Bruckner combines a high-bay warehouse with covered fleet parking. Vice chairman Leslie Lanne, SVPs Jeremy Liebler and James Ferrigno and senior managing director Seth Geldzahler lead the JLL leasing team. “Companies serving New York have become far more sophisticated in how they think about their supply chains,” said Lanne. “Occupiers want facilities that shorten delivery windows, accommodate growing vehicle fleets and improve operating efficiency without sacrificing proximity to their customers. That’s exactly what 307 Bruckner was designed to deliver.” Located less than a mile from the RFK, Willis Avenue and Third Avenue bridges, with immediate access to both the Bruckner and Major Deegan expressways, 307 Bruckner offers rapid connectivity to a population of more than 16 million across Manhattan, Queens, Brooklyn, northern New Jersey and Westchester. The post Sterling Organization Nears Delivery of High-Bay Bronx Warehouse appeared first on Connect CRE.

stories.summary: Sterling Organization is nearing delivery of 307 Bruckner, a 100,000-square-foot industrial property in the Bronx scheduled for Q3 2026, combining high-bay warehouse space with covered fleet parking. Positioned less than a mile from three major bridges with express access to the Bruckner and Major Deegan expressways, the asset targets companies optimizing supply-chain efficiency and last-mile logistics serving a 16+ million population across the tri-state region. JLL's leasing team notes tenants increasingly prioritize warehouse design that shortens delivery windows and improves operational efficiency.
stories.impact: Bronx industrial supply is growing and absorbing tenants seeking proximity to Manhattan/NJ customer bases without premium Manhattan or Jersey City rents. This supply increase may moderate Bronx industrial pricing and cap rates, affecting multifamily development financing in Bronx submarkets if cap-rate compression reduces cross-collateral borrowing capacity. Monitor Bronx industrial absorption and rental growth; strong logistics demand supports daytime employment and transit ridership, which can boost nearby residential demand if residential supply remains tight.

stories.title: CBRE Arranges Full-Building Industrial Lease in Irvine
stories.excerpt: CBRE completed a full-building lease for 136,612 square feet to an undisclosed tenant at Irvine Commerce Center, a Class A industrial building located at 18582 Teller Ave. in Irvine. EVPs Ross Bourne and Ross Fippinger and senior associate Joe Czech represented the owner, an Ares Real Estate fund. Marq Logistics, which represents Ares’ vertically integrated global logistics real estate platform, developed Irvine Commerce Center and manages the property. The building includes 13,275 square feet of high-end office space with upgraded finishes, along with modern industrial features designed to accommodate a range of distribution and light manufacturing uses. Located along Jamboree Road in Irvine’s Airport Area submarket, the property provides immediate access to the Interstate 405 freeway and is near Newport Beach. The surrounding Irvine Business Complex offers a wide range of walkable amenities. “We continue to see sustained demand for high-quality industrial space across Orange County,” said Bourne. “The deal highlights the resiliency of the Airport Area industrial market.” Hear from the West Coast’s Leading Industrial Real Estate Experts | August 20Gain firsthand insight from the executives, investors, and developers navigating today’s industrial market. For multifamily developers, strong warehouse absorption near Irvine Business Complex signals robust local employment and suggests residential demand uptick in adjacent Irvine submarkets, supporting rental growth assumptions.

stories.title: Clarion Partners Acquires Grocery-Anchored Fairfield County Retail

The purchase price was not disclosed. JLL represented the seller, a joint venture between Sagehall Partners and The Prusik Group. Located in densely populated Fairfield County, Main Avenue Shopping Plaza is fully leased to a roster of nationally recognized retailers led by Stop & Shop, Hobby Lobby, and Total Wine & More. The 16-acre property has served the local community for nearly three decades and benefits from a prominent location at the intersection of Main Avenue, U.S. Route 7, and the Merritt Parkway “This acquisition reflects continued conviction in well-located, grocery-anchored retail centers that provide durable cash flow and potential long-term value creation,” said Clarion Transactions VP Taylor Epperson. “Main Avenue Shopping Plaza combines exceptional real estate fundamentals with a highly stable tenant roster serving an affluent and growing consumer base. The property’s strong occupancy, long-term leases and strategic location make it an excellent opportunity for our investors.” The post Clarion Partners Acquires Grocery-Anchored Fairfield County Retail appeared first on Connect CRE.

Strong retail anchors and demographics support nearby multifamily demand; multifamily developers in Norwalk/Fairfield County should view Clarion's purchase as validation of demographic resilience and consumer spending in the corridor, supporting rent-growth assumptions for new residential supply targeting affluent suburban cohorts.

stories.title: Bill Ackman Buys 125 West End Avenue for $260M Brain Research Institute
stories.excerpt: Billionaire hedge funder Bill Ackman has kicked off his $260 million play to establish a brain research institute on Manhattan’s Upper West Side. Pershing Square Foundation, the philanthropic arm of Ackman’s fund, dropped $188 million to acquire 125 West End Avenue, according to city documents filed Tuesday. The 400,000-square-foot life sciences building planned for the site will eventually host Ackman’s massive brain research center, the Ackman Oxman Institute, Fortune first reported. The sale by Taconic Partners reportedly precedes another in-contract sale for the neighboring building, 320 West 66th Street, for roughly $70 million. Together, the acquisitions would secure Pershing Square Foundation an estimated 700,000 square feet of research and office space between West 65th and West 66th streets. Ackman told Fortune that the charitable venture was inspired by his 26-year-old daughter, Lucy, who previously suffered a brain hemorrhage, as well as his wife, Neri Oxman, who lost her mother to Alzheimer’s disease. Pershing Square Foundation has teamed up with Mount Sinai Hospital System to develop the research institute, although the development timeline is unclear. The life sciences and office spaces at 125 West End Avenue, also called West End Labs, appear largely vacant, according to the building’s website. The building belongs to a 3.4-acre campus, known as West End Campus, sold to Taconic by Silverstein Properties for $230 million in 2019. West End Campus also includes 320 West 66th Street and a vacant parcel. Taconic repositioned the campus as a purpose-built research and laboratory complex. Its previous lives include the American Broadcasting Company (ABC)’s former campus, a Chrysler Motor Company facility and printing facilities for The New York Times. Spokespeople for Pershing Square Foundation and Taconic did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Bill Ackman/Pershing Square Foundation $188M acquisition of 125 West End Avenue, Manhattan

stories.summary: Pershing Square Foundation, the philanthropic arm of billionaire hedge funder Bill Ackman, acquired 125 West End Avenue on Manhattan's Upper West Side for $188 million to develop a 400,000-square-foot life sciences building housing the Ackman Oxman Institute for brain research. A second in-contract acquisition of 320 West 66th Street (approximately $70 million) will bring the combined research and office footprint to roughly 700,000 square feet between West 65th and West 66th Streets.
stories.impact: Major institutional life sciences capital inflow to Upper West Side signals long-term institutional commitment to that corridor; brain research institute will anchor high-earning professional workforce and increase daytime population density. Multifamily developers should monitor life sciences campus development and resulting talent in-migration; the institute may catalyze residential demand from research professionals and support rent growth in nearby Upper West Side apartments, particularly studios, one- and two-bedroom units targeting young scientists and researchers.

stories.title: Goulston & Storrs Adds Brian Grindall to Real Estate Practice
stories.excerpt: Brian Grindall, a veteran commercial real estate attorney who spent nearly 16 years at Tenenbaum & Saas in Washington, D.C., has joined law firm Goulston & Storrs, Commercial Observer has learned. Grindall has been added to Goulston & Storrs’ real estate group as a director in the firm’s Washington, D.C., office. In addition to his time at Tenenbaum & Saas where he ascended to partner, Grindall was previously a general counsel at development firm the Opus Group, according to his Linkedin profile. “Brian has built an impressive practice advising clients on their most significant transactions,” Paul Tummonds Jr., director and administrative head of Goulston & Storrs’ D.C. office, said in a statement. “His experience, practical business perspective, and ability to navigate complex real estate matters make him an outstanding addition to our firm.” In his more than two-decade legal career, Grindall has advised CRE parties on a variety of deals including acquisitions, dispositions, financing, leasing and development. His practice also involves advising on joint ventures, loan workouts and restructuring of distressed properties. Grindall earned his master’s in real estate from Johns Hopkins University, his law degree from New England Law and his B.A. from the College of Wooster. “Goulston & Storrs has built an outstanding real estate platform and a reputation for delivering practical, business-focused counsel,” Grindall said in a statement. “I was drawn to the firm’s collaborative culture and the opportunity to work alongside a team that shares my commitment to helping clients solve complex real estate challenges.” Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.

stories.summary: Commercial real estate attorney Brian Grindall, who spent 16 years as partner at Tenenbaum & Saas in Washington, D.C., and previously served as general counsel at development firm Opus Group, joined law firm Goulston & Storrs as director of the D.C. real estate practice. Grindall's expertise spans acquisitions, dispositions, financing, leasing, development, joint ventures, and loan workouts across major CRE transactions.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily supply, demand, or capital markets. Lateral hire reflects healthy legal services demand in Washington, D.C., CRE market and may signal elevated transaction volume. Developers with Washington, D.C., portfolios or planned DC market entries should note Grindall's move may enhance Goulston & Storrs' capability to serve multifamily clients in the region, but does not signal market-wide demand shifts.

stories.title: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs Takes 5K SF at 1733 Eastchester Road in the Bronx
stories.excerpt: Simone Development Companies has brought its two-story, 27,275-square-foot medical and office building at 1733 Eastchester Road in the Bronx’s Morris Park neighborhood to full occupancy, according to the firm. The building’s last vacant space was leased in June, when the U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) inked a long-term, 5,234-square-foot lease to house the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs’ new Bronx Vet Center at the property. It was a direct lease between the GSA and Simone. The Bronx vet center will provide counseling, outreach and referral services to veterans and service members, as well as their families. The Department of Veterans Affairs has several other vet centers in New York City, including locations in Ridgewood, Queens, Downtown Brooklyn and in Midtown. The asking rent in the deal was not disclosed, but the average asking rent for office space in the Bronx was $39.46 per square foot during the second quarter of 2026, according to research by PropertyShark. The vet center’s lease brought Simone’s 1733 Eastchester Road to full occupancy after the landlord also signed a 2,766-square-foot lease in May with Downtown Brooklyn Physical Therapy to open the medical service provider’s first Bronx location. The length of that lease and the asking rent were not disclosed. Simone was also represented in-house in this deal, while the tenant was represented by Gary Mayzlin from Real Estate Trade Company. Mayzlin did not immediately respond to a request for comment. “The full lease-up of 1733 Eastchester Road reflects the growing need for well-located and high-quality outpatient medical and social services space in the Bronx,” Joe Simone, president of Simone, said in a statement. “We’re thrilled that the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs and Downtown Brooklyn PT chose this property, which offers great visibility, modern professional space, and a strategic location to accommodate the expanding needs of these vital service providers.” Other tenants at 17

stories.summary: Simone Development Companies achieved 100% occupancy at its two-story, 27,275-square-foot medical and office building at 1733 Eastchester Road in the Bronx's Morris Park neighborhood when the U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) signed a long-term lease for 5,234 square feet to house a U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs Vet Center. stories.title: Whole Foods Signs 8K-SF Lease to Open Daily Shop at 1524 Second Avenue
stories.excerpt: Whole Foods Market has signed a lease on the Upper East Side to open its version of a mini-mart. The Amazon-owned grocery chain closed an 8,121-square-foot deal for one of its small-scale concepts on the ground floor of ConTowers Associates LP’s 1524 Second Avenue, also known as the Continental Towers, according to landlord broker Newmark. While the brokers did not define what kind of concept the store will be, the focus will be on prepared foods in a convenient setting. It will likely be part of the grocer’s Whole Foods Market Daily Shop concept, which launched in March 2024. Newmark did not disclose the length of the lease, but said the asking rent was $250 per square foot. “This transaction presented a unique opportunity to secure a highly visible corner location in one of Manhattan’s most established neighborhood retail corridors,” Newmark’s Jeffrey Roseman, who represented the landlord alongside Drew Weiss, said in a statement. “The combination of the property’s location, visibility and surrounding residential density made it an excellent fit for Whole Foods Market’s neighborhood store format.” Chase Welles and Jacqueline Klinger of The Shopping Center Group negotiated on behalf of Whole Foods, but did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Whole Foods has been expanding its daily shop presence in New York City lately, signing a ​​15-year, 10,000-square-foot lease at 1224 Flushing Avenue in Bushwick, Brooklyn, in June for the bodega-branded concept. In January, however, the e-commerce giant announced it would close all of its Amazon Go and Amazon Fresh locations in an effort to focus on Whole Foods as a brand and on its online grocery delivery services. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.

stories.summary: Whole Foods Market, owned by Amazon, signed an 8,121-square-foot lease at 1524 Second Avenue (Continental Towers) on Manhattan's Upper East Side to open a Daily Shop concept focused on prepared foods. The ground-floor location offers high visibility in an established neighborhood retail corridor. The asking rent was $250 per square foot.
stories.impact: Whole Foods Daily Shop expansion signals Amazon's confidence in Upper East Side retail fundamentals and shopper convenience needs; the smaller-format concept targets daytime office workers and nearby residential customers. Upper East Side retail velocity and rent absorption ($250/SF ground-floor) indicate healthy leasing demand; multifamily developers in Upper East Side residential buildings should view grocery/prepared-foods retail as a positive amenity co-signal supporting residential rents and tenant satisfaction in luxury and market-rate buildings.
